idiom_name: immutable snapshot + structural sharing ({...state, k: v}); single owner per agent, message passing between agents, Atomics only on SharedArrayBuffer
implementation_notes: JavaScript gives the pattern's effect rather than its structure: object copies are shallow and made with spread/Object.assign/structuredClone, so the idiom is to build a new immutable snapshot per update and hand that snapshot to whoever reads, keeping the unchanged subtrees - exactly what the COW handle spends a reference count to avoid. Thread-safety is the runtime's: the main thread and each worker have separate object graphs, so there is no shared counted body to protect, and values cross agents only by structured clone or as views over a SharedArrayBuffer - and Atomics are 'used with SharedArrayBuffer and ArrayBuffer objects', i.e. numeric shared memory only. A hand-written counted handle is not expressible here (no deterministic destruction, no user-visible reference counts), so the classic form is justified only behind a WebAssembly/native boundary, not in idiomatic JavaScript. This is not a discouraged case: the observable effect - cheap copies, readers that never block, consistent snapshots - is achievable with ordinary language features.
pitfalls: Spreads are shallow: {...state} still points at the same nested object, so an in-place mutation of a nested value is visible to every reader holding the old snapshot - freeze the leaves or re-create the changed path explicitly.

Snapshots are only shared inside one agent: postMessage structured-clones objects (no shared references), so a worker cannot observe a snapshot published on the main thread; only SharedArrayBuffer views are truly shared, and their constructor is gated behind cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP).

Object.freeze is shallow and sloppy-mode silent: freezing the top object does not freeze nested values, and an assignment to a frozen property fails without a runtime error (or throws in strict mode/module code), so immutability stays a convention.
sources: MDN, Atomics - 'static methods for carrying out atomic operations ... used with SharedArrayBuffer and ArrayBuffer objects', with wait/notify modelled on futexes: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Atomics

MDN, SharedArrayBuffer - postMessage/structured cloning gives the receiver a 'new, private SharedArrayBuffer object' over the same data block, and the constructor is hidden unless the document is cross-origin isolated: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SharedArrayBuffer
